Module 2. Preparing and exploring longitudinal data in R

Answer key

source(here::here("R", "setup.R"))
walk <- load_walk()

This answer key gives complete, executed solutions to the Module 2 workbook, model answers to the written questions and marking notes.

WarningSimulated data

All examples use simulated data from fictional studies. Results illustrate methods; they are not empirical findings.

baseline <- load_walk("baseline")
wide     <- load_walk("wide")
sched_months <- c(0, 1, 3, 6, 9, 12)

1 Guided exercises

1.1 Exercise 1. Reshaping between wide and long (LO 2.1)

long_from_wide <- wide |>
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("sbp_m"),
               names_to = "month_sched", names_prefix = "sbp_m",
               names_transform = list(month_sched = as.numeric),
               values_to = "sbp")
nrow(long_from_wide)
#> [1] 2160
sum(is.na(long_from_wide$sbp))
#> [1] 263
check <- long_from_wide |>
  filter(!is.na(sbp)) |>
  full_join(walk |> select(id, month_sched, sbp_long = sbp),
            by = c("id", "month_sched"))
nrow(check)
#> [1] 1897
sum(is.na(check$sbp) | is.na(check$sbp_long) | check$sbp != check$sbp_long)
#> [1] 0
steps_wide <- walk |>
  select(id, arm, month_sched, steps) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = month_sched, values_from = steps,
              names_prefix = "steps_m")
dim(steps_wide)
#> [1] 360   8
head(steps_wide, 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#>   id    arm   steps_m0 steps_m1 steps_m3 steps_m6 steps_m9 steps_m12
#>   <chr> <fct>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 W001  EP         4.5      6.5      7.7      7.2      7         8.2
#> 2 W002  SP         7.5      7.8     NA       NA       NA        NA  
#> 3 W003  UC        11.2      9        9        7.7     10.8       9.5
steps_wrong <- walk |>
  select(id, arm, month_sched, month, steps) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = month_sched, values_from = steps,
              names_prefix = "steps_m")
dim(steps_wrong)
#> [1] 1897    9

Answers.

  1. 2160 rows: 360 participants × 6 scheduled visits. Of these, 263 are NA (visits not attended), leaving 1897, the number of rows in walk_long.csv. The join in (b) finds no disagreements.
  2. With month kept, every row has a unique combination of id and month, so pivot_wider() cannot collapse a participant’s visits into one row. The result has 1897 rows (one per visit) instead of 360, mostly filled with NA.
  3. Each wide column corresponds to one scheduled visit, and the column name holds the time. Actual times differ between participants, so they cannot be column names. To keep them you need a second set of columns (month_m0, …, month_m12), or better, keep the data in long format.

Marking notes. Accept names_transform = list(month_sched = as.integer) or parse_number(). A common error is leaving month_sched as text, which sorts "12" before "3".

1.2 Exercise 2. Joining and validating (LO 2.2)

walk_joined <- walk |>
  left_join(baseline |> select(id, rand_date, sbp0, dropout),
            by = "id", relationship = "many-to-one")
c(before = nrow(walk), after = nrow(walk_joined))
#> before  after 
#>   1897   1897
nrow(anti_join(walk, baseline, by = "id"))
#> [1] 0
nrow(anti_join(baseline, walk, by = "id"))
#> [1] 0
walk_bad <- walk |> mutate(id = if_else(id == "W004", "w004", id))
joined_bad <- walk_bad |>
  left_join(baseline |> select(id, rand_date), by = "id")
sum(is.na(joined_bad$rand_date))
#> [1] 6
anti_join(walk_bad, baseline, by = "id") |> distinct(id)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>   id   
#>   <chr>
#> 1 w004
names(left_join(walk, baseline, by = "id")) |> grep(pattern = "\\.x|\\.y", value = TRUE)
#>  [1] "clinic.x" "arm.x"    "age.x"    "sex.x"    "bmi.x"    "clinic.y"
#>  [7] "arm.y"    "age.y"    "sex.y"    "bmi.y"

Answers.

  1. The row count is unchanged (1897), so no visit was duplicated. No visit lacks a baseline record, and every randomised participant has at least one visit.
  2. Neither: a left join with an unmatched key runs silently and fills the new columns with NA. Here 6 rows (all of W004’s visits) have a missing rand_date. Without anti_join() you would notice only by counting NA values in the joined columns, or later, when actual time could not be computed. Adding unmatched = "error" to the join makes it stop.
  3. Shared variables other than id are duplicated with suffixes (clinic.x, clinic.y, arm.x, arm.y and so on). Code that refers to arm then fails, or worse, uses the wrong copy. Select the new columns only, or join by all shared columns.

1.3 Exercise 3. Cleaning the raw export, part 1 (LO 2.3)

raw <- read_csv(here("data", "walk_visits_raw.csv"),
                col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
step2 <- raw |>
  mutate(id          = toupper(trimws(participant)),
         month_sched = as.numeric(sub("^M", "", visit_label)),
         visit       = match(month_sched, sched_months),
         visit_date  = as.Date(visit_date, format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
         sbp         = parse_double(sbp_mmhg),
         steps       = parse_double(steps_k)) |>
  select(id, visit, month_sched, visit_date, sbp, steps)
stopifnot(all(grepl("^W[0-9]{3}$", step2$id)), !anyNA(step2$visit))
n_exact <- sum(duplicated(step2))
n_exact
#> [1] 6
step3 <- distinct(step2)
nrow(step3)
#> [1] 1900
conflicts <- step3 |>
  add_count(id, visit, name = "n_records") |>
  filter(n_records > 1)
conflicts
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   id    visit month_sched visit_date   sbp steps n_records
#>   <chr> <int>       <dbl> <date>     <dbl> <dbl>     <int>
#> 1 W255      5           9 2024-12-12   129   7.7         2
#> 2 W290      2           1 2024-11-21   136   5.9         2
#> 3 W290      2           1 2024-11-23   140   5.9         2
#> 4 W216      2           1 2024-07-20   143   7.7         2
#> 5 W216      2           1 2024-07-22   137   7.7         2
#> 6 W255      5           9 2024-12-14   139   7.7         2
step4 <- step3 |>
  group_by(id, visit) |>
  mutate(conflict_flag = n() > 1) |>
  arrange(visit_date, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup()
nrow(step4)
#> [1] 1897

Answers.

  1. Duplicates are found by comparing values. w004 and W004 are different strings, so a copy of a record that differs only in the case of the ID would not be detected, and the participant would appear to have two different records.
  2. 6 exact duplicate rows and 3 conflicting visits (6 records). After resolving them, 1897 rows remain.
  3. A rule chosen after seeing which version of each record benefits which arm is part of the analysis, not of the data management, and it can push the estimated treatment effect in the direction the analyst prefers. Prespecifying the rule (in the data management or statistical analysis plan, before unblinding) means that the result cannot depend on the analyst’s expectations. Even when the effect is tiny, as here, the principle protects the credibility of the trial.

Marking notes. Full marks for question 3 require the idea that the choice could bias the treatment comparison and that the safeguard is prespecification or blinded review. Accept other prespecified rules (closest to target date, average) if they are justified and applied without reference to outcomes.

1.4 Exercise 4. Cleaning the raw export, part 2 (LO 2.3)

step5 <- step4 |>
  left_join(baseline |> select(id, rand_date), by = "id",
            relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  mutate(days     = as.numeric(visit_date - rand_date),
         month    = round(days / 30.44, 2),
         dev_days = as.numeric(visit_date - (rand_date + round(month_sched * 30.44))))
range(step5$days)
#> [1]   0 405
step6 <- step5 |>
  mutate(sbp_flag = case_when(is.na(sbp) ~ "blank",
                              sbp < 70 | sbp > 250 ~ "implausible",
                              TRUE ~ "ok"),
         sbp_raw = sbp,
         sbp = if_else(sbp_flag == "implausible", NA_real_, sbp))
step6 |> filter(sbp_flag != "ok")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 13
#>   id    visit month_sched visit_date   sbp steps conflict_flag rand_date   days
#>   <chr> <int>       <dbl> <date>     <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>         <date>     <dbl>
#> 1 W088      6          12 2025-02-20    NA   4.2 FALSE         2024-02-09   377
#> 2 W345      1           0 2024-08-26    NA   9.9 FALSE         2024-08-26     0
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: month <dbl>, dev_days <dbl>, sbp_flag <chr>,
#> #   sbp_raw <dbl>
window_days <- c(`0` = 0, `1` = 7, `3` = 14, `6` = 28, `9` = 28, `12` = 28)
walk_clean <- step6 |>
  mutate(out_of_window = abs(dev_days) > window_days[as.character(month_sched)])
walk_clean |> count(month_sched, out_of_window) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = out_of_window, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   month_sched `FALSE` `TRUE`
#>         <dbl>   <int>  <int>
#> 1           0     360      0
#> 2           1     314     10
#> 3           3     304     15
#> 4           6     309      0
#> 5           9     294      3
#> 6          12     282      6
agreement <- walk_clean |>
  full_join(walk |> select(id, visit, month_ref = month, sbp_ref = sbp),
            by = c("id", "visit"))
sum(is.na(agreement$month_ref)); sum(is.na(agreement$month))
#> [1] 0
#> [1] 0
agreement |> filter(is.na(sbp) | sbp != sbp_ref) |>
  select(id, visit, sbp, sbp_raw, sbp_ref)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   id    visit   sbp sbp_raw sbp_ref
#>   <chr> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 W088      6    NA    1190     119
#> 2 W345      1    NA      NA     152
table(round(agreement$month - agreement$month_ref, 2))
#> 
#> -0.02 -0.01     0  0.01  0.02 
#>    72   471   829   454    71
bad <- walk_clean |> filter(sbp_flag == "implausible")
cleaning_log <- tibble(
  step = c("Rows read", "Exact duplicate rows removed",
           "Visits with conflicting records (earliest kept)",
           "Rows after de-duplication", "Blank SBP values",
           "Implausible SBP values set to missing",
           "Out-of-window visits (kept, flagged)"),
  n = c(nrow(raw), n_exact, n_distinct(paste(conflicts$id, conflicts$visit)),
        nrow(walk_clean), sum(walk_clean$sbp_flag == "blank"),
        nrow(bad), sum(walk_clean$out_of_window)))
knitr::kable(cleaning_log)
step n
Rows read 1906
Exact duplicate rows removed 6
Visits with conflicting records (earliest kept) 3
Rows after de-duplication 1897
Blank SBP values 1
Implausible SBP values set to missing 1
Out-of-window visits (kept, flagged) 34

Answers.

  1. One blank value (W345, baseline) and one implausible value (W088, month 12, recorded as 1190 mmHg). The blank is a missing value at an attended visit and is left missing, with a query to the clinic. The value 1190 is impossible for a living adult and is almost certainly 119 typed with an extra zero, but the WALK plan does not allow corrections by assumption, so it is set to missing, the raw value is kept, and a query is raised. If the clinic confirms 119, the source data are corrected.
  2. 34 visits are out of window. They should be kept and flagged. They are genuine measurements taken at a different time. Excluding them would create extra missing data, and the course models place each measurement at its actual time. A sensitivity analysis excluding them is reasonable.
  3. The raw visit dates were created as the randomisation date plus round(month * 30.44) days, so they are rounded to whole days. Recomputing month from a whole-day date cannot recover the original two-decimal value, and differences of up to 0.02 months (under one day) result. They are harmless. The recomputed month is the correct time for the recorded date.
  4. See the cleaning log above.

Marking notes. Accept “correct to 119” only if the participant explicitly states it as a documented rule (for example “obvious transcription errors are corrected and logged”) and keeps the raw value. Deduct if the participant deletes the row entirely: the visit was attended and steps were measured.

1.5 Exercise 5. Missing visits, summaries and flow (LO 2.3, LO 2.4)

grid <- baseline |>
  select(id, arm) |>
  crossing(visit = 1:6) |>
  mutate(month_sched = sched_months[visit]) |>
  left_join(walk |> select(id, visit, sbp), by = c("id", "visit")) |>
  mutate(observed = !is.na(sbp)) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(last_seen = max(visit[observed]),
         miss_type = case_when(observed ~ "observed",
                               visit < last_seen ~ "intermittent",
                               TRUE ~ "after dropout")) |>
  ungroup()
count(grid, arm, miss_type) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = miss_type, values_from = n)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   arm   `after dropout` intermittent observed
#>   <fct>           <int>        <int>    <int>
#> 1 UC                 71           21      628
#> 2 SP                 58           20      642
#> 3 EP                 74           19      627
visit_flow(walk, id, month_sched, arm) |>
  left_join(count(baseline, arm, name = "randomised"), by = "arm") |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", n_seen, 100 * n_seen / randomised)) |>
  select(arm, month_sched, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = cell)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   month_sched UC         SP         EP        
#>         <dbl> <chr>      <chr>      <chr>     
#> 1           0 120 (100%) 120 (100%) 120 (100%)
#> 2           1 107 (89%)  107 (89%)  110 (92%) 
#> 3           3 106 (88%)  110 (92%)  103 (86%) 
#> 4           6 101 (84%)  103 (86%)  105 (88%) 
#> 5           9 99 (82%)   102 (85%)  96 (80%)  
#> 6          12 95 (79%)   100 (83%)  93 (78%)
mean_sd <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(x), sd(x))
baseline |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(n = as.character(n()), Age = mean_sd(age),
            `Female, n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", sum(sex == "Female"),
                                      100 * mean(sex == "Female")),
            BMI = mean_sd(bmi), `SBP, mmHg` = mean_sd(sbp0),
            `Steps, 1000/day` = mean_sd(steps0)) |>
  pivot_longer(-arm, names_to = "Characteristic") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = value) |>
  knitr::kable()
Characteristic UC SP EP
n 120 120 120
Age 59.6 (9.4) 60.1 (8.3) 60.5 (9.2)
Female, n (%) 65 (54%) 68 (57%) 57 (48%)
BMI 28.6 (4.0) 30.0 (4.2) 29.3 (4.4)
SBP, mmHg 146.2 (12.6) 147.2 (14.1) 147.5 (13.2)
Steps, 1000/day 6.0 (2.4) 6.1 (2.1) 5.9 (2.4) 
walk |>
  group_by(arm, month_sched) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean = round(mean(sbp), 1), sd = round(sd(sbp), 1)) |>
  print(n = 18)
#> # A tibble: 18 × 5
#> # Groups:   arm [3]
#>    arm   month_sched     n  mean    sd
#>    <fct>       <dbl> <int> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 UC              0   120 146.2  12.6
#>  2 UC              1   107 143.4  11.7
#>  3 UC              3   106 142.7  12.2
#>  4 UC              6   101 142.9  12.4
#>  5 UC              9    99 143.6  12.6
#>  6 UC             12    95 144.3  13.3
#>  7 SP              0   120 147.2  14.1
#>  8 SP              1   107 144.2  14.3
#>  9 SP              3   110 141.4  14.1
#> 10 SP              6   103 140    14  
#> 11 SP              9   102 139    13.8
#> 12 SP             12   100 139.6  13.1
#> 13 EP              0   120 147.5  13.2
#> 14 EP              1   110 142.6  13.6
#> 15 EP              3   103 139    12.9
#> 16 EP              6   105 136.1  13.1
#> 17 EP              9    96 136.8  13.3
#> 18 EP             12    93 136.6  12.7

Answers.

  1. The long file contains only attended visits. A participant who was randomised but never seen, or a visit that nobody attended, has no row and would be missing from a grid built from the data. The randomisation list and the protocol schedule define what should exist.
  2. 263 of 2160 scheduled visits (12.2%) are missing, of which 203 (77% of the missing visits) follow dropout.
  3. In a randomised trial any baseline difference between arms is due to chance by construction, so a test only checks the randomisation and its p-value has no useful interpretation. What matters is whether sex is prognostic for SBP. If it is, adjust for it (prespecified), whatever the size of the baseline difference.

1.6 Exercise 6. Exploratory plots (LO 2.5)

walk_lab <- walk |>
  mutate(arm_lab = factor(walk_arm_labels[as.character(arm)],
                          levels = walk_arm_labels))
p1 <- plot_spaghetti(walk_lab, month, sbp, id, group = arm_lab, alpha = 0.15) +
  labs(x = "Months since randomisation", y = "SBP (mmHg)")
p2 <- plot_spaghetti(walk_lab, month, sbp, id, group = arm_lab, n_show = 30,
                     seed = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Months since randomisation", y = "SBP (mmHg)")
p1 / p2
set.seed(4)
panel_ids <- baseline |> group_by(arm) |> slice_sample(n = 4) |> pull(id)
walk_lab |>
  filter(id %in% panel_ids) |>
  ggplot(aes(month, sbp, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, ncol = 4) +
  scale_colour_arm(name = NULL, labels = walk_arm_labels) +
  labs(x = "Months since randomisation", y = "SBP (mmHg)")
plot_observed_means(walk_lab, month_sched, sbp, arm_lab) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sched_months) +
  labs(x = "Scheduled month", y = "Observed mean SBP (mmHg)")
plot_missing_map(grid, id, visit, observed, order_by = last_seen) +
  facet_wrap(~ arm, scales = "free_y", labeller = as_labeller(walk_arm_labels)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = sched_months) +
  labs(x = "Scheduled month")
walk |>
  left_join(baseline |> select(id, last_month_sched), by = "id") |>
  group_by(arm, last_month_sched, month_sched) |>
  summarise(mean_sbp = mean(sbp), n = n()) |>
  ggplot(aes(month_sched, mean_sbp, colour = factor(last_month_sched))) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
  facet_wrap(~ arm, labeller = as_labeller(walk_arm_labels)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#D55E00", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73",
                                 "#CC79A7", "#222222"),
                      name = "Last seen (month)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sched_months) +
  labs(x = "Scheduled month", y = "Mean observed SBP (mmHg)")

Answers.

  1. Mostly in level. The spread between participants at any visit (tens of mmHg) is much larger than the change over time within the arms (a few mmHg on average). Individual lines also fluctuate from visit to visit.
  2. All arms show a fall over the first three months, largest in the enhanced programme and smallest in usual care, followed by a plateau (with a slight rise in usual care). Change is not linear in time.
  3. Mainly monotone dropout (the staircase at the bottom of each panel) with a smaller number of scattered intermittent missed visits.
  4. Participants who leave early tend to start higher: at baseline, those last seen at month 3 or earlier had mean SBP 154.9 mmHg (n = 39) against 146 mmHg (n = 321) for the others. Caution is needed because most patterns contain fewer than ten participants per arm, so their means are noisy, and each pattern’s profile covers only the visits before dropout.

Marking notes. Any reasonable choice of colours or subset size is acceptable if the subset is random with a fixed seed. Deduct for plotting individual trajectories against scheduled time without comment, or for hand-picking participants.

2 Independent exercises

2.1 Exercise 7. How much does the duplicate rule matter? (LO 2.3)

conf_rows <- step3 |>
  semi_join(conflicts, by = c("id", "visit")) |>
  left_join(baseline |> select(id, arm, rand_date), by = "id") |>
  mutate(dev = abs(as.numeric(visit_date - (rand_date + round(month_sched * 30.44)))))
rules <- conf_rows |>
  group_by(id, arm, visit) |>
  summarise(earliest = sbp[which.min(visit_date)],
            closest  = sbp[which.min(dev)],
            average  = mean(sbp))
rules
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#> # Groups:   id, arm [3]
#>   id    arm   visit earliest closest average
#>   <chr> <fct> <int>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 W216  EP        2      143     143     140
#> 2 W255  SP        5      129     139     134
#> 3 W290  EP        2      136     136     138
alt_means <- function(rule) {
  step3 |>
    anti_join(conflicts, by = c("id", "visit")) |>
    bind_rows(rules |> ungroup() |> transmute(id, visit, sbp = .data[[rule]])) |>
    left_join(baseline |> select(id, arm), by = "id") |>
    semi_join(rules, by = c("arm", "visit")) |>
    group_by(arm, visit) |>
    summarise(mean_sbp = mean(sbp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(rule = rule)
}
rule_means <- bind_rows(lapply(c("earliest", "closest", "average"), alt_means)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = mean_sbp)
rule_means |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   arm   visit earliest closest average
#>   <fct> <int>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 SP        5    139.0   139.1   139.0
#> 2 EP        2    142.6   142.6   142.6
max_shift <- with(rule_means, max(abs(c(closest - earliest, average - earliest))))

Model answer. The rules disagree for some visits. For W255 the record closest to the target date is the later one, so “earliest” and “closest” keep different values, and averaging gives a third value. The arm means at the affected visits change by at most 0.1 mmHg, because only one or two of about 100 values per arm and visit are affected. A suitable data management plan statement: “When two records exist for the same participant and visit, the clinic will be asked to confirm the correct record. If the query cannot be resolved, the earliest-dated record will be used and the visit flagged. This rule is fixed before unblinding and will be applied without reference to treatment arm or outcome values.” The rule must be fixed in advance because a choice made after seeing its consequence for the arm comparison could, deliberately or not, favour one arm.

Marking notes. Accept any of the three rules if justified. The key marks are for showing the sensitivity, and for the explanation of prespecification.

2.2 Exercise 8. Steps over time (LO 2.4, LO 2.5)

steps_summary <- walk |>
  group_by(arm, month_sched) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(steps), sd = sd(steps))
steps_summary |> mutate(across(c(mean, sd), \(x) round(x, 2))) |> print(n = 18)
#> # A tibble: 18 × 5
#> # Groups:   arm [3]
#>    arm   month_sched     n  mean    sd
#>    <fct>       <dbl> <int> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 UC              0   120  6     2.38
#>  2 UC              1   107  6.11  2.43
#>  3 UC              3   106  6.21  2.28
#>  4 UC              6   101  6     2.27
#>  5 UC              9    99  6.18  2.45
#>  6 UC             12    95  6.28  2.38
#>  7 SP              0   120  6.05  2.06
#>  8 SP              1   107  6.78  1.95
#>  9 SP              3   110  7.23  1.93
#> 10 SP              6   103  7.24  2.12
#> 11 SP              9   102  7.18  1.91
#> 12 SP             12   100  7.25  2.24
#> 13 EP              0   120  5.89  2.36
#> 14 EP              1   110  6.96  2.12
#> 15 EP              3   103  8     2.12
#> 16 EP              6   105  8.17  2.27
#> 17 EP              9    96  8.09  2.02
#> 18 EP             12    93  7.96  2.11
p_m <- plot_observed_means(walk_lab, month_sched, steps, arm_lab) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sched_months) +
  labs(x = "Scheduled month", y = "Mean steps (1000/day), 95% CI")
p_s <- plot_spaghetti(walk_lab, month, steps, id, n_show = 30, seed = 3,
                      alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(x = "Months since randomisation", y = "Steps (1000/day)")
p_m + p_s

Model answer. Mean steps start at about 6 thousand per day in all arms (6.0, 6.1 and 5.9 in UC, SP and EP). They rise quickly after randomisation in the programme arms, to about 7.3 (SP) and 8.0 (EP) thousand per day at month 12, most of the rise occurring by month 3, and change little in usual care (6.3). Participants differ widely: the standard deviation at each visit is about 2 thousand steps per day, as large as the rise in the enhanced programme’s mean, and individual lines fluctuate from visit to visit.

2.3 Exercise 9. Who drops out? (LO 2.5, LO 2.6)

baseline_t <- baseline |>
  mutate(sbp0_third = cut(sbp0, quantile(sbp0, c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1)),
                          include.lowest = TRUE,
                          labels = c("Lowest third", "Middle third", "Highest third")))
drop_tab <- baseline_t |>
  group_by(sbp0_third, arm) |>
  summarise(pct_dropout = round(100 * mean(dropout))) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = pct_dropout)
drop_tab
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#> # Groups:   sbp0_third [3]
#>   sbp0_third       UC    SP    EP
#>   <fct>         <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 Lowest third     20    10    24
#> 2 Middle third     18    24     9
#> 3 Highest third    26    18    36
overall_third <- baseline_t |> group_by(sbp0_third) |> summarise(p = 100 * mean(dropout))
complete <- load_walk("complete")
m12 <- complete |>
  filter(month_sched == 12) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(observed = mean(sbp[observed]), complete = mean(sbp)) |>
  mutate(difference = observed - complete)
m12
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   arm   observed complete difference
#>   <fct>    <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 UC       144.3    144.7    -0.3882
#> 2 SP       139.6    140.2    -0.5983
#> 3 EP       136.6    137.7    -1.086

Model answer. Dropout is most common among participants in the highest third of baseline SBP: 26%, against 18% in the lowest and 17% in the middle third (all arms together). Within arms the pattern is irregular, because each cell holds only about 40 participants, but the highest third has the highest or second-highest dropout in every arm. Baseline SBP is only a proxy: in WALK dropout depends on the most recent observed SBP. Because participants with higher SBP are more likely to be missing at month 12, the observed month-12 mean is lower than the complete-data mean in every arm, by 0.4 to 1.1 mmHg. The comparison with walk_complete.csv is possible only because the data are simulated. In a real study you see only the first column, and the dropout table is the evidence that it is biased downwards.

2.4 Exercise 10. Out-of-window visits (LO 2.3, LO 2.5)

win <- tibble(month_sched = sched_months[-1],
              w = window_days[as.character(sched_months[-1])])
walk_clean |>
  filter(visit > 1) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(month_sched), dev_days)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = out_of_window), width = 0.2, height = 0, size = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(data = win, aes(x = factor(month_sched), ymin = -w, ymax = w),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, linetype = "dashed", width = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#9A9A9A", `TRUE` = "#D55E00"),
                      labels = c("Within window", "Out of window"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Scheduled month", y = "Deviation from target date (days)")
m12_window <- walk_clean |>
  filter(month_sched == 12) |>
  left_join(baseline |> select(id, arm), by = "id") |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(all_visits = mean(sbp, na.rm = TRUE),
            within_window = mean(sbp[!out_of_window], na.rm = TRUE),
            n_excluded = sum(out_of_window))
m12_window
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   arm   all_visits within_window n_excluded
#>   <fct>      <dbl>         <dbl>      <int>
#> 1 UC         144.3         144.6          3
#> 2 SP         139.6         139.4          3
#> 3 EP         136.8         136.8          0

Model answer. Deviations widen with follow-up. Because the windows also widen, most out-of-window visits are at months 1 and 3. Excluding the 6 out-of-window month-12 visits changes the arm means at month 12 by at most 0.2 mmHg, which does not change the description of the data. The course models use actual time (month) for the random slope, so a late visit is placed where it happened rather than discarded. That keeps the information and avoids creating extra missing data.
